questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 5 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 5 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 22 & 22 \\ 0 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{3}{22}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 22 & 22 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ 22{x}_{2}=22.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}+4(1)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-2+1=-1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing More Than Two Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 
The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{2}=4 \\ -{x}_{3}=-1 \\ 0=4,\end{aligned}
$$

where the fourth equation is always false. Therefore, the system has no solution and we conclude that 

$$
x\notin \text{Span}{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ -8 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ -8 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 8 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=10 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
4{x}_{1}+3\cdot 2=10\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1+2=3.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis by Inspection
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,-8\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,4\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}+{{(\,2\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{3}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=-8\cdot {b}_{1}+4\cdot {b}_{2}+2\cdot {b}_{3}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],
$$

Finally, ${x}_{2}=4.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis by Inspection
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,8\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=3\cdot {b}_{1}+8\cdot {b}_{2}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we have that ${x}_{1}=3.$
